clue.text: Fine places across America for particular people

indicators.note: across here means placed alongside, so the places word sits next to America

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine (as on pencil leads)
US is the abbreviation for the United States
spots are places, as in a nice spot

explanation.surface: A sign: fine places all over America for fastidious folk.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fussy is particular, and a fusspot is a person who frets over small details.

clue.text: Who may upset Rick?

indicators.note: upset means the letters of who may are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A question asking who might annoy a man called Rick.
explanation.walkthrough: Rick looks like a man's name, but here it is a stack of hay.
explanation.definitionFit: A rick is a stack of hay, and a haymow is hay heaped up for storage, synonyms in farming.

clue.text: One charged right out of club

indicators.note: out of says the letter for right is taken away from the club word

parts.note: an iron is a golf club

explanation.surface: Someone accused of a crime who has been expelled from a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One charged' suggests an accused person; it is electrical charge.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom or molecule carrying an electric charge is called this, a chemistry term.

clue.text: His legs'll be exercised in addition to winter transport!

indicators.note: exercised means the letters of his legs'll be are worked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A man's legs get a workout as well as his snowy vehicle, presumably pushing a sledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Bells are hung on a sledge as an extra to the vehicle, jingling as it moves over snow.

clue.text: Buoyant: no turning back after opening encounter

indicators.note: after says the buoyant word and the reversed no come behind the opening word

parts.note: an opening is an opportunity, a chance
buoyant spirits are up

indicators.note: turning back says the word no is read in reverse

explanation.surface: Cheerful advice: no going back after a first meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buoyant' looks like the definition at the start, but it only supplies part of the wordplay; the definition is 'encounter' at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To come across something by luck is to meet or encounter it, a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Horse, beginning slowly, canters and gallops

indicators.note: beginning asks for the opening letter of each of the next four words

explanation.surface: A horse starts slowly, then canters and gallops.
explanation.walkthrough: The racing picture misleads: 'Horse' is slang for heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse and scag are both slang names for heroin, so they are synonyms in drug slang.

clue.text: Did well: succeeded by accident

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees
a prang is British slang for a minor crash, usually a car bump

explanation.surface: Someone did well, then followed it with a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Did well' reads as succeeding, but it means welled up, as water does.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that wells up rises from the ground, as a spring does; the verb's past tense fits.

clue.text: Gift of article: I left it for Times to include

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: to include says the multiplying word goes round the other letters

parts.note: by means times in multiplication, as in three by four

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece in which the writer gave something to the Times to publish.
explanation.walkthrough: Times is not the newspaper: it is BY, as in multiplication.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift is a natural talent, and this word means a skill or talent, a close synonym.

clue.text: In addition, restriction involving small digit

parts.note: too means in addition, also

indicators.note: involving says the restriction word takes in the abbreviation for small

parts.note: a tie is a restriction or constraint

explanation.surface: A restriction on something involving a little finger.
explanation.definitionFit: A childish word for a toe, and a toe is a digit of the foot.

clue.text: Head of sprinkler on half cut hose

indicators.note: on says this letter follows the drunk word

parts.note: half cut is British slang for drunk, tight

indicators.note: head of picks the opening letter of sprinkler

explanation.surface: Fixing a sprinkler head on a garden hose that has been cut in half.
explanation.walkthrough: The garden picture misleads: 'half cut' means drunk, and hose is legwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Hose is an old word for stockings or leg coverings, of which tights are an example.

clue.text: Singer too taken with soloist's alternative tip

indicators.note: alternative tip says the other end of soloist, its final letter, replaces the first one

parts.note: also means too
S is the first tip of the word soloist

explanation.surface: A singer too, paired with the alternative favoured by a soloist.
explanation.walkthrough: Soloist has S at one tip and T at the other; in the word for too, the S is swapped for T.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a singer with the voice range below soprano, so a singer in the choir.

clue.text: Gracious men backed and supported European assembly

parts.note: cor is an exclamation of surprise, like gracious!

indicators.note: backed says the soldiers' abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers, so men
bore means supported, carried

explanation.surface: Polite men back and support a European parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gracious' looks like an adjective for men; it is the exclamation COR.
explanation.definitionFit: A corroboree is an Australian Aboriginal ceremonial gathering, so a kind of assembly.

clue.text: It's anyone's guess, sadly, how snake's strangled archdeacon

indicators.note: strangled says the jumbled letters wrap round the archdeacon's title
sadly says the letters of how snake are disordered

parts.note: how snake, with the 's read as has, joining it to strangled
Ven, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: Nobody can say how a snake came to throttle a churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of snake's is 'has': the anagram of HOW SNAKE has strangled VEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for saying that nobody knows or can tell the answer.

clue.text: Oddly neglected term for musical genre

indicators.note: oddly neglected says the odd letters of term for are dropped, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A strange forgotten name for a style of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Emo is a style of emotional rock music, an example of a genre.

clue.text: Order shoddy goods: little one can return

indicators.note: return says the pair of words is read backwards

parts.note: tat is cheap, shoddy goods
a kid is a little one, a child

explanation.surface: Buy poor-quality goods, and a child can send them back.
explanation.definitionFit: A diktat is a decree imposed without consultation, so an order.

clue.text: Old shed visited by grandmother periodically

indicators.note: visited by says the grandmother word goes in among the other letters

parts.note: to doff is to take off or shed, as a hat
nan is a grandmother

explanation.surface: Granny pops into an old garden shed from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: Shed looks like a garden hut, but it is the verb, DOFF.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening intermittently, at intervals, happens periodically.

clue.text: Lake circled by songbird and quail

indicators.note: circled by says the songbird goes round the lake letter

parts.note: a finch is a songbird

explanation.surface: A lake ringed by songbirds and quail, a bird scene.
explanation.walkthrough: With a songbird about, 'quail' reads as a bird; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To quail is to shrink back in fear, so a verb synonym for wince or recoil.

clue.text: Light source of merriment in the daily round

parts.note: the Sun is a British daily newspaper

indicators.note: in says that letter goes inside the round

parts.note: a lap is a round of a track

indicators.note: source of picks the opening letter of merriment

explanation.surface: A light source of fun in everyday routine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British daily tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp giving ultraviolet rays for tanning gives off light, so it is a light in the sense of a lamp.

clue.text: After tea, is drug provided for coach?

parts.note: post means after, as in postwar
cha is slang for tea
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A question about whether, after tea, drugs are given to a sports coach.
explanation.walkthrough: Coach looks like a trainer; it is a carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A post-chaise was a horse-drawn carriage hired for travel, a historical kind of coach.

clue.text: On the job training with glue, ultimately quick work

indicators.note: training means the letters of on the job and glue are drilled into a new order
ultimately picks the final letter of quick

explanation.surface: Learning on the job with glue, which in the end makes for quick work.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's collection of stories is a literary work, an example of the word.

clue.text: Priest and sailor live together

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
to be is to live, exist

explanation.surface: A priest and a sailor share a home.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbé is the French title for a priest or cleric.

clue.text: Prophet's series of abnormal achievements

indicators.note: series of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A prophet with a string of extraordinary feats.
explanation.definitionFit: Malachi is the last of the Old Testament minor prophets; Prophet's reads as prophet is.

clue.text: Letters and form picked up for US family members

indicators.note: picked up says the words are heard, taken in by ear

parts.note: letters is Ys, the letter Y more than once, and form is guise

explanation.surface: Letters and forms collected for American relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a Mafia family are known in American slang as made men or wiseguys.

clue.text: Sentiment, comparatively silly, almost nobody finds welcome

parts.note: goo is sickly sentiment
dafter is the comparative of daft, silly

indicators.note: almost says the last letter of the word for nobody is dropped

parts.note: no one means nobody

explanation.surface: Nobody, near enough, finds a rather silly sentiment welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: A greeting used in the middle of the day is a form of welcome.

clue.text: A little matter of boss going off with husband

indicators.note: off means the letters of boss going are gone wrong, rearranged

explanation.surface: A small matter of the boss leaving with her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little matter' seems like a small issue; it is a particle of matter.
explanation.definitionFit: This subatomic particle is a tiny bit of matter in physics, so a punning description.

clue.text: On the wagon, long trailer keeps getting connected

indicators.note: keeps says the trailer word holds the other pieces

parts.note: an ad, advertisement, can be a trailer for a film
TT means teetotal, off alcohol
to ache is to long for

explanation.surface: A long trailer behind a wagon is hitched up.
explanation.walkthrough: The wagon is not a vehicle: being on the wagon means being teetotal, TT.
explanation.definitionFit: Attached and connected both mean joined or fastened on, synonyms.

clue.text: Blooming foul, what majors do to captains!

parts.note: flowers that are out are blooming
rank means foul smelling

explanation.surface: An exclamation that what majors do to captains is a disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' looks like a mild swear word; it means flowering.
explanation.definitionFit: A major is senior in rank to a captain, so stands above one in the hierarchy.

clue.text: Ruin hill training with party

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill
PE is physical education, training
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Hill training with a party would ruin things.
explanation.definitionFit: To torpedo plans is to wreck or sink them, a figurative sense.

clue.text: Drive extremists from theatre: force enemy to retreat

indicators.note: extremists from picks the end letters of theatre
to retreat says force and enemy are read backwards

parts.note: a foe is an enemy

explanation.surface: Drive the radicals out of a theatre, forcing the enemy to retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: Drive looks like 'expel'; it is a golf stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, to start a hole is to make the first drive from the tee.

clue.text: Second class help to get the Head demoted

indicators.note: get the head demoted says the first letter is moved down to the end

parts.note: to abet is to help

explanation.surface: A second-class assistant gets the headteacher demoted.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta is a second-class grade in marking, after alpha.
